Alas, R-style matrix or vector slicing (indexing with e.g. 1:4) is not allowed (yet). As far as I understand it, you have to assign each element separately. Bummer.

By the way, it seems you are only using assigning a data-value to x_a_pos once, and then it doesn't change anymore. You should move this to the transformed data block (and just do it once) and save overhead (now it's being done every darn leapfrog step).

Could you explain why i should initialize them in transformed?  What is the benefit of doing that?

If my assumption about x_a_pos only holding a constant value obtained from data is true (I haven't look close enough at all the code), you should only need to do it once. And you can. In the transformed data block. Anything that's in the model block gets executed every leapfrog step (so most likelily multiple times per iteration), so if you are calculating constants over and over again, you're wasting time. Again, Bob may have a more comprehensive explanation (including stuff about expensive gradient calculations etc.), but this should be reason enough to move things to transformed data block.

parts:
append_row is like rbind and append_col like cbind in R.
If you have

vector[M] x; // M x 1
vector[N] y; // N x 1
vector[M + N] x_cat_y; // (M + N) x 1

x_cat_y <- append_row(x, y);

You are adding more rows because vector is a column-vector
by default. This would also be legal:

vector[M] x; // M x 1
vector[M] y; // M x 1
vector[M,2] m; // M x 2

m <- append_col(x, y);

You append two column vctors of the same size to get
an (M x 2) matrix (2 columns and M rows).

- Bob
